ROUND-3 FINDINGS
- R3-1 resolved. I re-ran every AC14 command on a fresh copy of the current sai/ tree: npm ci, HOME=<tmp>.
  - Package pin: `jq -S -c --arg k pixel-office 'del(.scripts[$k])'` gives 5c59292586d92e95c1ea507ef7a46790a125677172c3fe3abfd90dedd9edf0a4. That equals my round-3 form; the quote-free form is right for YAML.
  - From tools/, `npx prettier --find-config-path src/pixel-office/public/index.html` exits 1 («Can not find configure file»). It works before the file exists.
  - The rules and globals print-config hashes match: 856ee001..., bec0f88d....
  - Pinned file hashes match: .prettierignore cd446cc5..., lockfile 92d27c4e..., .gitignore 4d56952b... (content «node_modules/»).
  - Greps: the word grep exits 1. The widened directive grep exits 1 on tools/src and tools/test, and 2 as written until tools/src/pixel-office exists (intended). The skip/todo grep exits 1.
  - npm run check exits 0: 115/115, «skipped 0», «todo 0»; no .sai-pixel-office in the temp HOME.
- tools/.gitignore pin (ORCH-approved addition): correct and needed. Probes on a scratch copy:
  - an entry «src/pixel-office/» in tools/.gitignore makes prettier --check . exit 0 on an unformatted file (control 1). find-config-path does not see it (exit 1); the pin does (437a1871 instead of 4d56952b);
  - a parent sai/.gitignore or sai/.prettierignore has no effect (exit 1), so tools/ is the only place to pin.
- R3-2 resolved.
  - The description states the tie behaviour exactly: k forged lines at F, m real lines before F − 120 s; real lines marked while m ≤ k, and one forged line is enough; forged lines marked from m = k + 1; permanent if no more real lines land before F − 120 s.
  - AC4 (б) says «среди непомеченных строк … помеченная строка из конфликтов выбывает».
  - AC13 puts the limit in README «### Ограничения», with the grep strings «одной вписанной строки» and «навсегда».
  - I re-derived it: forged and real lines form a complete bipartite conflict set; forged degree m, real degree k; a tie marks the later line. My round-3 cases B and C match the text: k=1/m=1 wrong, k=1/m=2 right, k=2/m=2 and k=3/m=3 wrong, m=k+1 right; B3, B4 and B6 permanent.
- R3-3 resolved.
  - AC4 (б) states the one-pass test: a conflict exists iff some line is more than 120 s earlier than the latest time before it.
  - The new tests: a generated journal of 100,000 accepted lines, and one with 5 forged lines (±1 h, at least 1,000 lines from the end). Each must take at most 1 s for the read rule plus the task list, with exactly 5 marked. «Числа» records 100,000 lines and 1 s.
  - Feasibility: the analyst's scratchpad/readrule-perf.mjs reproduces exactly — 16 ms and 37 ms, 5 marked, 0 mismatches against the literal rule over 300 journals.
  - Independently, the analyst's fast() matched my literal rule (val-r3-rule.mjs, written from the AC4 text) on 2,000 sparse, tie-heavy journals with 1-3 forged lines: 0 mismatches.

NOTE, NON-BLOCKING
H1 - REQ-001 AC14. The print-config hash commands list files with `find src test -name '*.js'`. ESLint also lints .mjs and .cjs by default (probe: a browser .mjs file fails lint without a globals block). A rules block for **/*.mjs with `"no-undef": 0` passes eslint, the *.js hash (856ee001 unchanged) and the word grep. So the parenthesis «любое изменение правил … в любом блоке меняет сумму» holds only while every JS file is .js.
The criterion itself stays decidable: «tools/eslint.config.js получает только блок с files и languageOptions.globals» is checked by reading the file. tools/ is "type": "module", so the page needs no .mjs.
Recommendation (ORCH's call; it can go into the design's test mapping):
  - use `-name '*.*js'` in both find commands. It is backslash-free, covers .js/.mjs/.cjs, gives the same 23 files and the same pinned hashes today, and catches the probe (6a3c71d1);
  - RELEASE-VALIDATOR also reads eslint.config.js against the stated property.
